transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-09-29
Time: 16:00 PDT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Nina Gonzalez (AstraCloud, Head of ML), Samir Khan (Platform), Priya Rao (Security), Eli Turner (Product)

Summary: quick scout to understand AstraCloud's inference needs across hosted/dedicated/private; heavy focus on open models, long context (40k+), multilingual support and tool-calling (external data pulls). Customer wants perf numbers and security docs before pilot.

[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros then we'll jump into what you're trying to do, timelines, and what success looks like for you.
[00:18] Nina (AstraCloud): hi all. I'm nina, head of ml. we have a roadmap item to add LLM features into our ops console — think incident summarization, multi-doc search, and a chat assistant. main asks are support for long context (we're thinking 20k-40k tokens for some flows), multilingual responses (en/es/pt), and ability to call internal tools/APIs securely. timeline is Q1 pilot.
[00:38] Ravi (Redwood SE): great, and what's your expected qps? are these interactive UI calls or async batch jobs?
[00:44] Samir (AstraCloud): mostly interactive, target p95 latency < 600ms for short prompts, but for the long context summarization we can accept higher latency — up to 2s token latency maybe — as long as cost is manageable. concurrency initially 10-20 qps.
[01:02] Maya: ok. so tradeoffs we'll look at: hosted for fastest start, dedicated for predictable throughput and isolation, private for full network isolation and KMS. any regulatory constraints that push you straight to private?
[01:15] Priya (AstraCloud): we need audit logs, KMS integration, SSO (SAML/Okta) and data residency controls. SOC2 is a must for vendor selection. so if hosted meets our audit/KMS needs and we can restrict data residency, it's acceptable — otherwise private.
[01:36] Ravi: noted. on models: are you leaning toward open models or proprietary APIs?
[01:40] Nina: open models — prefer to avoid per-call proprietary license costs. we want to evaluate Llama variants, Mistral-ish, and the newer long-context models; also exploring instruction-tuned mats. tool-calling is important — we need model to produce structured calls that our backend can execute.
[02:02] Ravi: cool. Redwood supports function/tool calling patterns and structured outputs. two practical things to surface: 1) long context performance depends on model architecture and runtime kernels; we can route long-context requests to models with optimized attention and to Dedicated hardware to keep latency consistent; 2) KV/prefix caching can drastically reduce cost for repeated context.
[02:28] Samir: when you say KV cache what's the expected hit rate we should plan for?
[02:32] Ravi: depends on user behavior; with session-based conversations you can get 60–80% reuse on recent tokens. for docs ingestion use-case, prefix caching of embeddings + doc chunks helps; we'll include guidance in the benchmark.
[02:48] Nina: and quantization? how much perf gain, and any quality regressions?
[02:52] Ravi: 8-bit quantization usually reduces memory and can run on more cost-efficient instances; for some open models quality delta is small, for others you'll want to validate with eval sets. Redwood Optimize can suggest per-model quant profiles. we'll include quantized vs fp16 numbers in the bench.
[03:12] Eli (AstraCloud): tool calling — we need to be sure the model won't hallucinate call names or params. can we force strict schemas?
[03:20] Ravi: yes, we support structured output schemas and function signatures. you can validate on the platform and fall back to a verification step. also we have retries and circuit-breakers in the routing policy for external calls.
[03:36] Priya: network egress: if we go private, can we keep traffic on-prem or in our VPC?
[03:42] Maya: private deployment supports VPC-only access and optional on-prem package. we integrate with KMS/HSM for key control and provide audit logs. we'll share the architecture doc and SOC2 artifacts.
[03:56] Nina: curious about multilingual: do we need separate models for ES/PT or is one model fine?
[04:02] Ravi: some of the mixed-lingual LLMs perform well across latin languages, but language-specific fine-tuning helps. we recommend a two-phase approach: polyglot model for baseline, then eval for high-volume languages to determine if a language-specific model is needed.
[04:18] Samir: latency targets again — can dedicated meet 600ms p95 for short prompts with long KV cache enabled?
[04:24] Ravi: yes, with Dedicated reserved GPU pools you can hit consistent latency — we'll show profiling. Hosted can also meet it at low concurrency but burst behavior differs. Dedicated gives you SLA and predictable throughput.
[04:40] Nina: what do you need from us to run the benchmark?
[04:44] Maya: sample prompts, sample documents (the 40k token style), multilingual examples, and ideally a small set of realistic user sessions. we'll do a 2-hour run with the same workload and return CSVs for latency/cost/token breakdown.
[04:56] Priya: send the security packet. we need SOC2, ISO certs, SSO flows, and audit log examples. also, encryption in transit and at rest details.
[05:06] Maya: yes — we'll attach SOC2 + architecture + KMS notes and a short note on network topologies for private deployment.
[05:12] Ravi: a couple of gotchas from other customers — with very long contexts the runtime selects different kernels and memory patterns; for some models you need to adjust batch sizes to avoid OOM. we'll recommend batch windows and autoscale profiles.
[05:28] Eli: how do rollouts work if we want to test a new model in prod for 5% of traffic?
[05:33] Ravi: Redwood Console supports canary/A-B with automatic fallback to previous model or region. you can set quality monitors tied to prompt sets and auto-roll back on regressions.
[05:44] Nina: competitors — we've talked to Anthropic and looked at Anthropic's long context roadmap; OpenAI is expensive for high volume. we're also testing some Replicate hosts for custom weights.
[05:57] Maya: good context — we'll include comparative notes and a suggested path: polyglot open model -> dedicated pilot -> language-specific tuning.
[06:06] Samir: anything else operational we should be aware of?
[06:09] Ravi: observability — token-level costs, per-route latency, tracing hooks to map a model call to your request id, and alerts for quality regressions. for tool calling we recommend an allowlist of external endpoints.
[06:26] Maya: ok quick recap and next steps: Maya sends pricing and pilot terms; Ravi runs bench; Priya gets security docs; Eli provides prompts; follow-up tech deep dive next week.
[06:36] Nina: thanks, that sounds good.
[06:39] Maya: thanks everyone. we'll post the bench link and a short one-pager.

End of meeting.

References / artifacts mentioned:
- Redwood Dedicated capacity + pricing (link to deck)
- SOC2 and architecture note (we'll attach to email)
- Benchmark plan template and CSV after run
- Sample prompts requested (EN/ES/PT)

Notes on transcript quality: a few mis-heard acronyms (one mention of "Mistral-ish" got transcribed as "mister-ish"), occasional filler words and overlap.
